quickStart: For an immediate emergency in Hong Kong, call 999.
Review emergency contacts, health details, legal document locations, insurance, bank accounts, MPF, pensions, and essential liabilities.
If someone has died, identify the executor or authorised representative and use the Hong Kong Judiciary Probate Registry and provider instructions.
Hong Kong probate grants cover Hong Kong estate assets; overseas property may need separate administration under the relevant jurisdiction.
Use official bank, MPF, IRD, and service-provider bereavement processes. Do not access accounts or use credentials without authority.
Keep the export encrypted. Never store passwords, iAM Smart or eTAX credentials, authentication codes, or recovery keys in it.

legalNotes: This guide is general information, not legal, tax, insurance, or financial advice.
Hong Kong has its own identity, healthcare, MPF, tax, probate, and property systems; do not apply another country's rules to Hong Kong assets.
HKID particulars are sensitive personal data. Record only what is necessary and share it only with organisations that need it.
Hong Kong public healthcare and private healthcare are distinct; eligibility and charges depend on status and service rules.

The Hong Kong Probate Registry explains that probate, letters of administration, or letters of administration with will annexed may be required. Hong Kong grants cover Hong Kong estate assets; overseas assets may require separate administration.
MPF death benefit claims are administered under the MPF system. Confirm who may claim and which documents are needed with the trustee and MPFA.

Hong Kong salaries tax, profits tax, property tax, and estate-duty questions depend on circumstances and relevant dates. Confirm current IRD guidance rather than relying on fixed thresholds in this organizer.
Official: Hong Kong health system overview: https://www.gov.hk/en/residents/health/hosp/overview.htm
Official: Hong Kong Judiciary Probate Registry: https://www.judiciary.hk/en/court_services_facilities/probate.html

Store credentials in a reputable password manager with an emergency-access feature, not in this export.

Use encrypted storage and secure channels for sensitive documents.
Review after major life events and at least annually; remove outdated copies securely.

recoveryRoadmap.description: A general checklist after a death in Hong Kong. Confirm authority, domicile, estate location, and current court and provider requirements before acting.

meta.title: Family Recovery Roadmap - Hong Kong
meta.reviewedBy: Government sources reviewed; case-specific legal and tax advice may be needed

intro.condolence: We are sorry for your loss. This checklist is intended to make the first practical steps clearer.
intro.howToUse: Register the death, identify the executor or administrator, notify relevant agencies and providers, and keep a record of each action.

startHere: Follow the official death-registration process and obtain the records requested by providers.
Locate the will and identify the executor; confirm whether a Hong Kong grant is required.
Notify banks, MPF trustees, insurers, employers, IRD, and other providers through their official bereavement processes.
List Hong Kong and overseas assets separately; confirm jurisdiction, ownership, and authority before changing accounts or distributing property.
Keep a log of contacts, forms, and documents supplied. Never use another person's iAM Smart, eTAX, or banking credentials.
legalFramework: Hong Kong Judiciary Probate Registry grants and estate administration.
The Hong Kong Probate Registry's jurisdiction is limited to estate assets in Hong Kong; overseas assets follow the applicable local process.
MPF scheme and trustee claim rules for a member's death.
IRD salaries, profits, property, and any relevant estate-duty rules.
Hong Kong identity, healthcare, and legal-document rules; seek advice for cross-border domicile or estate issues.

phases.title: Register and establish authority
phases.focus: Follow registration instructions, locate the will, and identify who may act.

keyActions.action: Follow the Immigration Department's death-registration instructions and obtain the documents needed by each institution.
keyActions.why: Registration and evidence requirements depend on circumstances and the receiving organisation.

keyActions.action: Find the will and confirm the executor; get legal advice for intestacy, disputes, or overseas property.
keyActions.why: A grant may be needed before the estate representative can administer assets.

mustHaveDocuments: Bank, MPF, insurance, property, and liability references
criticalMistakes: Assuming a relative can operate accounts without authority
Assuming Hong Kong probate covers overseas assets
Putting passwords or authentication codes in an export

phases.title: Notify and identify claims
phases.focus: Notify government agencies and providers and preserve an asset and liability inventory.

keyActions.action: Contact each MPF trustee and ask what estate representative documents and claim forms are required.
keyActions.why: MPF death claims follow MPF rules and trustee requirements.

keyActions.action: Contact banks, insurers, employers, IRD, lenders, property managers, and utilities separately.
keyActions.why: No single government notification completes all private account and benefit processes.

mustHaveDocuments: List of regular payments and liabilities
criticalMistakes: Assuming an MPF benefit or asset follows a will without checking

phases.title: Administer and finalise
phases.focus: Complete court, tax, property, and provider steps before final distribution.

keyActions.action: Confirm whether probate, letters of administration, or another grant is required for the Hong Kong estate.
keyActions.why: The required grant depends on the will, applicant, domicile, and estate assets.

keyActions.action: Check IRD filing or tax requirements and seek advice on cross-border assets or historical estate-duty questions.
keyActions.why: Tax and estate duties depend on dates, assets, and individual circumstances.

mustHaveDocuments: Hong Kong asset and liability inventory
criticalMistakes: Including overseas property in the wrong jurisdiction's filing
Assuming no tax or reporting steps apply

phases.title: Review family arrangements
phases.focus: Review the surviving household's will, incapacity documents, MPF, insurance, and secure recordkeeping.

keyActions.action: Review wills, enduring powers, advance directives, MPF information, insurance, and emergency contacts with appropriate professionals.
keyActions.why: Major life changes can make appointments and nominations outdated.
keyActions.legalRef: Hong Kong law and current MPF scheme requirements

keyActions.action: Keep an asset and digital-account index; store credentials only in a suitable password manager.
keyActions.why: A secure index helps authorised people locate records without exposing secrets.
